questions.question: 1. What two distinct physical mechanisms are combined to model the total base-emitter capacitance in SPICE?
2. The Forward Transit Time (`TF`) parameter is most closely related to which physical process?

answers.a: The time it takes for heat to dissipate from the junction.
answers.b: The time it takes for minority carriers to cross the base.
answers.c: The time it takes for the depletion region to form.
answers.d: The time it takes for the junction to break down under reverse bias.

questions.question: 3. A high-frequency BJT (a very fast transistor) would be expected to have what kind of Forward Transit Time (`TF`)?
4. When is the base-emitter *diffusion* capacitance at its largest value?

answers.a: When the transistor is in cutoff (off)
answers.b: When the B-E junction is reverse-biased
answers.c: When the transistor is heavily forward-biased (on)
answers.d: It is a constant value and does not change

questions.question: 5. When is the base-emitter *depletion* capacitance at its largest value?

answers.a: When the B-E junction is heavily reverse-biased
answers.b: When the B-E junction is heavily forward-biased
answers.c: When the collector voltage is at its maximum
answers.d: It is a constant value and does not change

questions.question: 6. For a B-E junction with a linearly graded doping profile, what value would be expected for the grading coefficient (`MJE`)?
7. For an abrupt (step) junction, which plot linearizes the C-V data to allow for parameter extraction?

answers.a: A plot of capacitance versus voltage
answers.b: A plot of the inverse of capacitance cubed versus voltage
answers.c: A plot of the inverse of capacitance squared versus voltage
answers.d: A plot of the log of capacitance versus voltage

questions.question: 8. From the slope of the *correct* linearized plot (e.g., inverse capacitance squared vs. voltage), what physical property can be extracted?
9. How does the B-E depletion capacitance change as the *reverse bias* on the B-E junction is increased?

answers.a: It increases, as the depletion region shrinks.
answers.b: It decreases, as the depletion region widens.
answers.c: It stays the same, as it is a fixed property.

questions.question: 10. Which extracted parameter is the most critical for modeling the high-frequency *gain* (fT) of the transistor?
